source:
Create a AAA-quality endless runner for Roblox inspired by the fast-paced gameplay of classic endless runners like Temple Run 2. The experience should capture the same adrenaline, fluid movement, exploration, and progression while using entirely original characters, environments, animations, music, sounds, UI, and level assets.
The game should feel polished enough to compete with top Roblox experiences.
Core Gameplay
Create an endless runner where the player automatically runs forward.
The player can:
 • Swipe Left → Turn Left
 • Swipe Right → Turn Right
 • Swipe Up → Jump
 • Swipe Down → Slide
 • Collect coins
 • Dodge obstacles
 • Navigate branching paths
 • Achieve high scores
 • Complete missions
 • Unlock cosmetics and characters
Movement should be smooth and highly responsive.

Motion Controls
On supported mobile devices, add optional motion controls using the device's accelerometer and gyroscope.
Features:
 • Tilt left/right to steer or subtly change lane position
 • Optional head-look camera effect
 • Motion sensitivity slider
 • Calibration screen
 • Toggle motion controls on/off
 • Automatic fallback to swipe controls if motion sensors are unavailable
 • Low-latency filtering to reduce jitter
 • Dead zones and smoothing for comfortable play
Motion controls should enhance gameplay without replacing core swipe controls.

Endless World Generation
Implement procedural generation that creates an endless path while maintaining handcrafted quality.
Include diverse original environments such as:
 • Ancient jungle ruins
 • Mountain temples
 • Lava caverns
 • Ice canyons
 • Desert ruins
 • Floating islands
 • Bamboo forests
 • Waterfalls
 • Forgotten cities
 • Underground caverns
Generation should avoid impossible obstacle combinations and maintain fair difficulty.

Obstacles
Create a large variety of original obstacles:
 • Gaps
 • Broken bridges
 • Fallen trees
 • Rolling boulders
 • Rotating blades
 • Swinging axes
 • Spike traps
 • Crumbling floors
 • Fire traps
 • Moving platforms
 • Collapsing bridges
 • Narrow ledges
 • Climbing sections
 • Rope swings
 • Zip lines
Difficulty should scale naturally as the run progresses.

Collectibles
Implement:
 • Coins
 • Rare gems
 • Power crystals
 • Treasure chests
 • Mystery relics
 • Keys
 • Daily collectibles
 • Seasonal collectibles

Power-ups
Create an extensible power-up system including:
 • Coin magnet
 • Temporary shield
 • Speed burst
 • Double coins
 • Slow-motion
 • Invincibility
 • Extra life
 • Auto-collect
 • Lucky treasure boost
Each should include:
 • Visual effects
 • Audio feedback
 • UI timers
 • Upgrade paths

Enemy Chase
Create an original pursuing creature that keeps pressure on the player.
Features:
 • Dynamic catch-up system
 • Difficulty scaling
 • Different chase phases
 • Escape mechanics
 • Cinematic introductions
 • Intelligent obstacle interaction

Missions
Implement hundreds of procedurally generated missions such as:
 • Collect coins
 • Travel distance
 • Jump count
 • Slide count
 • Near misses
 • Perfect turns
 • Consecutive runs
 • Power-up usage
 • Treasure collection

Progression
Create long-term progression:
 • Character unlocks
 • Outfit customization
 • Cosmetic trails
 • Pets
 • Skill upgrades
 • Permanent upgrades
 • Daily rewards
 • Weekly events
 • Achievements
 • Prestige system

Graphics
Create high-quality original visuals featuring:
 • Dynamic lighting
 • Volumetric fog
 • Weather
 • Water effects
 • Particle systems
 • Animated foliage
 • Day/night cycle
 • Cinematic camera
 • Smooth animations
 • Optimized performance across devices

Audio
Compose completely original music inspired by adventurous orchestral and tribal themes.
Include:
 • Ambient exploration music
 • Chase music
 • Menu music
 • Victory sounds
 • Coin collection
 • Power-ups
 • Environmental ambience
Do not use copyrighted music.

Roblox Features
Integrate:
 • DataStore
 • ProfileService
 • Leaderboards
 • Badges
 • Daily rewards
 • Cloud saves
 • Cross-device support
 • Mobile optimization
 • Console support
 • PC support

Performance
Optimize for:
 • 60+ FPS on modern devices
 • Graceful quality scaling
 • Streaming Enabled compatibility
 • Efficient procedural generation
 • Object pooling
 • Minimal memory usage

Code Architecture
Use clean, modular Luau code with separate systems for:
 • Runner Controller
 • Input Manager
 • Motion Control Manager
 • Procedural Generation
 • Obstacle Manager
 • Collectible Manager
 • Mission System
 • Progression System
 • Save Manager
 • UI Framework
 • Audio Manager
 • Camera Controller

QA & Polish
Do not stop after the first playable version.
Continue iterating by:
 • Automatically testing every gameplay mechanic
 • Verifying procedural generation never creates impossible paths
 • Stress-testing long runs
 • Testing all motion controls across supported devices
 • Optimizing performance
 • Eliminating bugs
 • Refining animations, controls, camera, and game feel
Repeat testing and refinement until the experience is polished, performant, and feels like a premium endless runner with original content suitable for Roblox.

answers.ask: How long should one generated stretch be before the biome changes?
answers.answer: Use short, readable biome stretches of roughly 60–90 seconds of running before transitioning to the next environment, with a brief blended transition segment.

answers.ask: How often should the path fork, and do the forks rejoin or commit the player to a branch?
answers.answer: Present a fork about every 20–30 seconds on average, and have branches rejoin after a short alternate segment so runs remain procedurally manageable and fair.

Build each biome as a short, readable 60–90-second stretch, joined by brief blended transition segments. Arrange a clear central route with collectible trails and varied traversable hazards including gaps, broken or collapsing bridges, fallen trees, rolling boulders, rotating blades, swinging axes, spike and fire traps, crumbling floors, moving platforms, narrow ledges, climbing sections, rope swings, and zip lines. About every 20–30 seconds, split the route into branching paths that rejoin after short alternate segments. Use dramatic terrain, animated foliage, water, weather, fog, dynamic lighting, and day-to-night atmosphere, with a pursuing original creature visible behind the runner during chase sections.

## Genre

The dominant and sole genre is Infinite Runner. Adventure is the visual register, but automatic endless forward movement and reaction-timed procedural hazards define the game.

## Shape and preset

Use `lane-free` for continuous steering along a route that turns, forks, and rejoins. Match the Free Runner preset and expand it with moving hazards, collectible trails, power-ups, and chase pressure explicitly requested by the author.

## Config requirements

Use `chunk-modular` for axis-aligned procedural segments and `obstacle-jump` for gaps, broken bridges, trees, spikes, fire traps, and crumbling floors. Use `obstacle-moving` for boulders, blades, axes, platforms, and collapsing bridges. Use `hazard-kill` for lethal obstacles and the pursuing creature. Draw `terrain-relief`, `water-body`, and `island-cluster` as dramatic mountains, canyons, waterfalls, caverns, and floating islands. Blend original jungle ruins, mountain temples, lava caverns, ice canyons, desert ruins, bamboo forests, waterfalls, forgotten cities, and underground spaces.

## Layout requirements

Place `collectible-nodes` as coins, gems, crystals, chests, relics, keys, and event trails along readable safe and risk-reward lines. Place `powerup-buffs` in visible approach lanes. Place one `trigger-despawn` behind the active queue. Fork the route about every 20–30 seconds and rejoin branches after short alternates. Keep obstacle spacing speed-relative and every generated pattern clearable.

## Layout components

Generate 60–90-second biome stretches linked by brief blended transitions. Each stretch needs one central traversable route, occasional short rejoining branches, terrain and architecture unique to its biome, and selected hazards from the full requested set, including narrow ledges, climbs, rope swings, and zip lines. Keep water, foliage, fog, weather, lighting, and day-to-night atmosphere compositionally readable, with the pursuer visible behind during chase segments.

## Render order

Use `topdown`: validate chunk connections, branches, rejoins, and hazard clearance first, then dress the plan isometrically. The plan is authoritative because an impossible generated sequence ends the run unfairly.

## Scale, theme, and pipeline cost

The scale band is huge because the endless route rotates through nine substantial environments. The theme is premium original adventure spectacle. Use `P6` for valid procedural structure, `P2` for overhanging caverns and traversal structures, `P3` for outdoor-to-cavern transitions, and `CHECK` for layered open-air and water play around floating islands.
